title: Rolling power blocks
prescription: WEEKDAY 4am SESSION, outside, flat-to-rolling. 4 x 3 MINUTES at controlled-hard effort, with 2 min easy jog between each. Take every rise inside the block hard and hold steady on the flats - do not slow down when the ground levels out, that is the whole point. Effort target: hard but repeatable, you could speak 3-4 words and no more. Why 3-minute blocks instead of 60s hill reps: your rises top out around 30 seconds, so a 60s uphill rep does not exist on your route. Sustained blocks are the safer bet for a course with 294m of gain (organiser figure), because 3-minute efforts build climbing endurance whether the climbs turn out to be long or short. NOT VERIFIED: nobody has seen the actual gradient profile. Recce the course and this session gets rebuilt properly. Easy warm-up 10 min and cool-down 10 min either side. No descent loading here: all downhill work stays on the weekend terrain day.
opt_out: 10 min easy. Then 4 x 3 min controlled-hard over the rolling section, 2 min easy jog between. 10 min easy.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h, 1%. Then 4 x 3 min at 6-8% incline, 2 min walk between. 10 min easy.

title: STEEP HILL - the km 6 session (outdoors)
prescription: SATURDAY 29 AUG, PLAN CHANGE. The trail is a 30 minute drive and that drive is not happening today, so the trail moves to Sunday and the steep hill five minutes away takes this slot. That is the right swap, not a consolation. MEASURED FROM THE COURSE KML: Beerwah is decided by ONE climb, 800m at 9.8% average starting at the 4.6km mark, which is a third of the total gain in a single hit. Your rolling route is 5-6% and you already run it Tuesday and Thursday. A long steep hill is the closest thing you have to km 6, and it beats the treadmill on footing. So this is the km 6 session, arriving one week early and outdoors. ||  WE DO NOT KNOW THIS HILL'S NUMBERS. Record the run. Afterwards I will pull the length and the real gradient off the file and we prescribe from measurement instead of from the word 'steep'. ||  SESSION: 10-15 min easy on the flat sections around the base. Then 3 x 3 min uphill. Effort, not pace: controlled hard, the effort you could hold for about 10 minutes, breathing heavy but not ragged. Short stride, quick cadence, eyes up, drive from the hip. If the hill runs out before 3 minutes, start lower next rep. WALK the whole way down every time, no jogging down - the descent here is recovery, not training. Roughly 3-4 min between reps. title: TREADMILL CLIMB - the km 6 session

title: TRAIL DAY - Taper long run
prescription: RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. Race is 7pm at the end of January, and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4am problem. || ONE OF YOUR TWO WEEKEND SLOTS - take whichever day suits, the treadmill climb takes the other. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah is descending and 750m of it is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. Mostly easy throughout - the hard climbing happens on the belt, not here. || 12km easy trail with 3-4 strides late.
opt_out: 12km trail, easy throughout. Walk the steep climbs, run descents controlled.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session. This one has to be outside on real ground.
hr_note: Under 158 on the flat. Climbs by effort - let HR drift into Z3/Z4, walk if it will not settle, expect it back down within 60-90s of the ground levelling. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: TREADMILL CLIMB - the km 6 session
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most race-specific session you own. Warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h, 1%. Then 2 x 8 min at 10% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h (adjust so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute). Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%. WHY: Beerwah has one decisive climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is 5-7 minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years. Nothing outdoors near you replicates it. This belt does. Garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.
opt_out: Not an outdoor session - nothing local matches 800m at 10%. Swap it with your trail day instead.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7, 1%. Then 2 x 8 min at 10%, 3 min walk at 1% between. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: Taper reps
prescription: 4 x 90s hard w/ 90s jog. Same effort as Sharpen, half the volume.   ||  Do the hard efforts on your moderate rise. Hold or wear the light high enough to pick up spiderwebs strung across the path at head height - that is what catches people out.

hr_note: Ignore HR on the sprints - 20s efforts finish before HR catches up. Between reps walk until you can talk in sentences. title: RACE: BEERWAH@NIGHT 10km - 7:00PM
prescription: THE ONE. Official course: 294m gain (verified with the organiser listing). Distance listed as 10km; the ~10.4km figure is unconfirmed. Day plan: carb-heavy lunch, light carb snack ~4pm, caffeine ~250-400mg at 6pm, pre-load fluids + electrolytes (humid 25C+ start). WU: 15 min easy + drills + 3 strides, done by 6:45pm. START POSITION: seed yourself top 10 into the first single track - passing in torchlight is expensive. Pace the first climb conservatively. Power-hike anything too steep to run efficiently. NOT VERIFIED: the claim that the final 3km is mostly uphill and decides the race has never been checked against a real course profile - recce the course and this whole race plan gets rewritten from actual data. Water only on course. A goal: sub-50.
opt_out: Race day. Outside, obviously.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session.
